sentences.text: The brief facts relevant for disposal of the present petition are that on 15.11.2014 at around 12:08 AM, the police received a call that an old man with cardiovascular problem needs help as he cannot find a vehicle.
Police officials went to receive the caller in a PCR van bearing registration no. DL- 1CP-8278, make MPV-LIBRA-36, Innova (in short, "PCR van").
Thereafter, the said old man who was also blind was picked up by the police and was taken to Sanjay Gandhi Hospital, Delhi.
On the way the car bearing registration no. DL-1YE-0341, (in short "offending vehicle") took a wrong turn and dashed into PCR van.
The driver of the offending vehicle was apprehended who was under the influence of alcohol.
Due to the accident, PCR van sustained damages.
3. It is stated that FIR bearing No. 1265/2014 of PS Begum Pur, U/s 279 IPC was registered in this regard.

4. After obtaining the copy of petition, written statement has been filed on behalf of respondent no.1 stating that vehicle no. DL-1YE-0341 was duly insured with Oriental Insurance Company Limited vide Police No. 121500/31/2015/01/50020677 effective from 30.10.2014 to 29.10.2018.

R-1 was also in possession of valid driving license and fitness certificate of the MACT Case No. 647/2018 (FIR no.
1265/2014) Deputy Commissioner of Police v. Praveen Kumar and Anr.
Page no. 2 of 12 offending vehicle.

sentences.text: It is also submitted that the R-1 was driving his vehicle at moderate speed whereas the driver of the PCR van was driving at a high speed and in rash and negligent manner.
Further, R-1 was also not under the influence of alcohol as alleged by the petitioner which can be proved through FIR and Registration card where nothing of this sort has been mentioned.

5. Written statement has also been filed on behalf of respondent no. 2 i.e. Oriental Insurance Co.
Ltd. and, it is, interalia, submitted that the present petition is liable to be dismissed as the said accident has been caused due to sole negligence of the driver of PCR van.
Also, the driver of the insured vehicle was under the influence of alcohol and he was also not in possession of driving license.
The insurance company is not liable to pay any compensation as the accident has been occurred on account of the sole negligence of the petitioner.
ISSUES 6.

After completion of pleadings, following issues were framed by this Tribunal on 04.04.2019 :-
1.

Whether on 14/15.11.2014 at about 12:08 AM, at Sukhbir Nagar, Delhi, the PCR (MPV) Libra-36 got hit by offending vehicle no. DL-1YE-0341 which was being driven by Praveen Kumar in a rash and negligent manner?

OPP. 
2. Whether the petitioner/ injured is entitled for compensation, if so, to what amount and from whom?

OPP. 
3. Relief.

My issue wise findings in the case are as under :-
ISSUE NO.1 1.

Whether on 14/15.11.2014 at about 12:08 AM, at Sukhbir Nagar, Delhi, the PCR (MPV) Libra-36 got hit by offending vehicle no. DL-1YE-0341 which was being driven by Praveen Kumar in a rash and negligent manner? OPP.
16.

It is well settled that the procedure followed for proceedings conducted by an accident tribunal is similar to that followed by a civil court and in civil matters the facts are required to be established by preponderance of probabilities only and not by strict rules of evidence or beyond reasonable doubts as are required in a criminal prosecution.

The burden of proof in a civil case is never as heavy as that is required in a criminal case, but in a claim petition under the Motor Vehicles Act, this burden is infact even lesser than that in a civil case.

Reference in this regard can be made to the MACT Case No. 647/2018 (FIR no. 1265/2014) Deputy Commissioner of Police v.
Praveen Kumar and Anr.

sentences.text: The petitioner examined PW-3, Ct. Harbir Singh who was the driver of the PCR van, in order to prove the facts regarding the occurrence of accident.

PW-3 has clearly and categorically stated that at the relevant date, time and place the offending vehicle, being driven by R-1, took wrong turn near Jain Nagar and dashed into PCR van from front side and caused severe damage to the government vehicle.
Offending vehicle was immediately stopped and R-1 was apprehended.
In his cross-examination, PW-3 has categorically deposed that they were carrying blind heart patient in PCR van therefore, he was driving the PCR van in emergency at the speed of 80-100 kmph.
PW-3 was cross examined at length on behalf of insurance company and stood the test of cross examination.
PW-3 has disclaimed the suggestions of respondent no. 2 suggesting that he hit the offending vehicle due to his negligent driving.
None of the respondents could bring any material on record which was inconsistent with the version of the petitioner.
There is nothing on record which suggests that oral testimony of PW-3 could not be believed.
As such, this Tribunal finds it appropriate to hold that the oral testimony of PW-3 is reliable and trustworthy.

Therefore, an adverse inference on this aspect is also required to be drawn against the respondents in view of the law laid down in case of Cholamandalam M.S. General Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Kamlesh, reported in 2009 (3) AD (Delhi) 310.

the Tribunal is of considered opinion that R-1 is guilty of rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle at the relevant time leading to the accident in which PCR van sustained damages.

Therefore, the Insurance company is not liable to pay compensation.
